pages.text: Day 58. The $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$() works up from $(item)Lorentz Transforms$() and the $(item)Minkowski Lattice$() to the $(item)Metric$() and $(item)Riemann Curvature Tensors$() and finally the $(item)Einstein Field Core$().

The order follows the physics. First flat $(thing)Minkowski$() spacetime, where the $(thing)Lorentz transform$() says how lengths and times change between moving observers. Then gravity: the $(thing)metric$() measures distance in curved spacetime, the $(thing)Riemann tensor$() measures the curvature, and Einstein's equations tie that curvature to matter.

Why it matters: wormhole throats need an $(item)Einstein Field Core$(), and Alcubierre coils need $(item)metric tensors$(). Kugelblitz chambers can merge black holes into $(item)Gravitational Wave Crystals$() - the ripple of two horizons becoming one, frozen solid.
Lengths shrink and clocks slow as you approach light speed. This crystal is always moving at 0.99c.$(br2)Made in $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$().
g_μν: the rule for measuring distance in curved spacetime.$(br2)Made in $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$().
Matter tells spacetime how to curve; spacetime tells matter how to move. Both halves, in one core.$(br2)Made in $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$().
Space and time as one four-dimensional geometry, with light cones at every point.$(br2)Made in $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$().
How much a vector turns when carried around a small loop - curvature itself.$(br2)Made in $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$().
